concepts.title: Comparing the two dynamics formulations
concepts.description: The slide contrasts computational organization, not competing laws of motion.

concepts.title: Choosing a formulation for the stated purpose
concepts.description: The lecture motivates Lagrangian analytical insight and model-based/AI dynamics learning while acknowledging recursive Newton–Euler computation.
concepts.subtopic: Choosing a formulation for the stated purpose

concepts.title: What independent coordinates remove
concepts.description: Reduced coordinates account for the admissible motion, rather than claiming that joint reactions or losses do not exist.

concepts.title: Kinetic energy and net work
concepts.description: Doubling speed multiplies its square by four; starting or stopping requires the corresponding change in kinetic energy.

concepts.title: Translation plus COM rotation
concepts.description: COM translation and spin are separate contributions and must both be retained.

concepts.title: Matching angular velocity and inertia coordinates
concepts.description: A scalar energy is coordinate-independent only when the components entering its formula are transformed consistently.
concepts.subtopic: Matching angular velocity and inertia coordinates

concepts.title: Potential reference and integral direction
concepts.description: The stored potential equals work released by the conservative force when returning to the chosen reference.

concepts.title: Total energy is not the Lagrangian
concepts.description: The plus sign defines total mechanical energy; the minus sign defines the Lagrangian.
concepts.subtopic: Total energy is not the Lagrangian

concepts.title: Order of Euler–Lagrange differentiation
concepts.description: The time derivative acts on the velocity derivative of L, not directly on L or on the coordinate derivative.

concepts.title: The positive potential-gradient term
concepts.description: Potential contributes its positive coordinate gradient on the actuator-effort side of the energy equation.

concepts.title: The named dissipative extension
concepts.description: This item reports the specific source statement. It does not claim that all damping laws admit a single Rayleigh function.

concepts.title: Reading a source limitation without overgeneralizing
concepts.description: Preserve attribution: this is a statement made by the limited presentation, not a universal impossibility result. Questions about a specific extended formulation would need its assumptions and equations.
concepts.subtopic: Reading a source limitation without overgeneralizing

concepts.title: Sign of gravitational potential
concepts.description: The vector formula gives increasing potential with upward height when physical gravity points downward.

concepts.title: Constant energy references do not alter effort
concepts.description: Only changes of potential with configuration affect the generalized force, not an arbitrary zero of energy.
concepts.subtopic: Constant energy references do not alter effort

concepts.title: Mixed coordinates and effort units
concepts.description: Each coordinate’s effort is chosen so effort times its differential contributes work.

concepts.title: Independent coordinates and generalized velocity
concepts.description: Minimal joint coordinates remove redundant configuration variables; their time derivatives need not be Cartesian end-effector velocity.

concepts.title: Geometry fixes the gravitational sign
concepts.description: The printed potential and axes determine the convention. Do not import the later RP example’s upward-height angle unchanged.

concepts.title: Torsional spring energy and torque
concepts.description: The potential-gradient contribution appears positively in the required actuator equation, while the spring’s physical restoring torque is its negative.

concepts.title: A coordinate-independent kinetic coefficient
concepts.description: A partial derivative checks explicit dependence on one independent argument. It does not impose a zero velocity.

concepts.title: The zero right-hand side is an assumption
concepts.description: A homogeneous right-hand side means no separately applied actuator input, not absence of conservative forces.
concepts.subtopic: The zero right-hand side is an assumption

concepts.title: Deriving the actuator equation
concepts.description: Differentiate the energies before substituting: the spring gives kt theta and gravity gives −mgl cos(theta).

concepts.title: Computing applied torque with radians
concepts.description: The three signed contributions are calculated separately; the spring uses the angle in radians.

concepts.title: Initial free acceleration at zero spring deflection
concepts.description: Zero spring deflection does not imply mechanical equilibrium when gravity acts with a nonzero lever arm.
concepts.subtopic: Initial free acceleration at zero spring deflection

concepts.title: Equilibrium of spring and gravity
concepts.description: Static equilibrium means zero net torque, not necessarily zero stored energy or zero individual torque.

concepts.title: Matching the Newton moment equation
concepts.description: The Newton derivation and the Lagrangian derivation agree only when the coordinate direction and angular units are kept consistent.

concepts.title: Degrees in trigonometry versus radians in a spring law
concepts.description: A trigonometric calculator may accept degrees, but the stiffness unit explicitly requires radians.
concepts.subtopic: Degrees in trigonometry versus radians in a spring law

concepts.title: Conservative energy and applied power
concepts.description: Conservative spring and gravity terms exchange kinetic and potential energy. Applied torque changes the total through its power.

concepts.title: Zero-gravity torsional oscillation
concepts.description: This is a derived limiting case of the printed motion equation, not an additional force model.

concepts.title: What the RP distance d2 measures
concepts.description: The correct radius is needed in both rotational speed d2 thetadot1 and gravity height d2 sin(theta1).
concepts.subtopic: What the RP distance d2 measures

concepts.title: Why only Izz appears
concepts.description: A prismatic relative motion does not prevent inherited rigid-body angular motion.

concepts.title: Radial and tangential velocity contributions
concepts.description: Polar COM motion has one outward component and one perpendicular tangential component.

concepts.title: Building the rotational energy coefficient
concepts.description: A combines all motion caused by theta1, including the translating COM of the prismatic link.

concepts.title: Computing both kinetic-energy contributions
concepts.description: Do not omit COM spin or sliding translation when collecting the scalar system energy.

concepts.title: Maximum extension is a constant energy datum
concepts.description: The maximum-extension parameter sets the zero reference and is not a moving generalized coordinate.
concepts.subtopic: Maximum extension is a constant energy datum

concepts.title: When the chosen potential minimum is zero
concepts.description: The reference constant uses the largest downward reach, so smaller extensions need not have zero potential even when pointing down.
concepts.subtopic: When the chosen potential minimum is zero

concepts.title: Three derivative vectors in coordinate order
concepts.description: Differentiate with respect to the coordinates while holding generalized velocities independent.
concepts.subtopic: Three derivative vectors in coordinate order

concepts.title: Velocity derivatives of the RP kinetic energy
concepts.description: The velocity derivative gives generalized momentum; its subsequent time derivative produces inertial effort.
concepts.subtopic: Velocity derivatives of the RP kinetic energy

concepts.title: The product-rule origin of Coriolis coupling
concepts.description: A diagonal mass matrix may still depend on configuration, so differentiating generalized momentum produces coupling.
concepts.subtopic: The product-rule origin of Coriolis coupling

concepts.title: Sign of the radial squared-rate term
concepts.description: The negative radial rate term is required for inward centripetal acceleration at fixed radius, with positive actuator force defined outward.
concepts.subtopic: Sign of the radial squared-rate term

concepts.title: Reconciling the unclear lower mass-matrix print
concepts.description: Use mutually consistent source premises and retain the printing issue rather than treating the unclear symbol as a new physical model.
concepts.subtopic: Reconciling the unclear lower mass-matrix print

concepts.title: A diagonal M does not eliminate all coupling
concepts.description: Acceleration coupling, velocity coupling and gravity dependence are distinct features of a dynamic model.
concepts.subtopic: A diagonal M does not eliminate all coupling

concepts.title: Units of a mixed-coordinate mass matrix
concepts.description: A mixed-coordinate matrix need not have identical units in all entries; each row and column has a physical pairing.
concepts.subtopic: Units of a mixed-coordinate mass matrix

concepts.description: Evaluate M qddot, V and G independently, remembering that the second generalized effort is a force.

concepts.title: Reversing only the revolute rate
concepts.description: A Coriolis product responds to reversing one of its factors, whereas the centrifugal squared-rate term does not.

concepts.title: Centripetal effort at fixed radial coordinate
concepts.description: Holding a constant radius during rotation requires an inward force even though the generalized radial acceleration is zero.
concepts.subtopic: Centripetal effort at fixed radial coordinate

concepts.title: Static horizontal and vertical support
concepts.description: The same gravitational load projects differently onto rotational and translational joint freedoms.

concepts.title: Angular momentum with zero gravity and input torque
concepts.description: No applied torque about theta1 conserves its generalized momentum, even while a radial actuator changes the rotational inertia.
concepts.subtopic: Angular momentum with zero gravity and input torque

sourceIssues.description: The slide does not explicitly state the conservative-force/path-independence condition for U(r). Questions using the force integral state that condition instead of treating an arbitrary force as admitting a position potential.

The blanket statement that gyroscopic and non-potential forces cannot be handled is not established as a universal result by the displayed restricted energy formulation. Retain explicit slide attribution if examined; do not teach it as a general impossibility of all generalized-force formulations. The dL/partial q mixed numerator typography is clarified by consistent page437 notation.

The torque-only label for tau applies to all-revolute coordinates. The next page includes prismatic coordinates, and the RP final equations explicitly include a force; mixed-coordinate questions distinguish N·m and N.

The angle-arc arrow alone is not a sufficient sign convention. Questions state theta positive from +X toward downward +Y, consistent with the displayed gravitational potential −mgl sin(theta), and assume the torsional spring is undeflected at theta=0.
The final equality to zero silently specializes the preceding equation with applied torque tau to the unforced case. Generated questions state tau=0 explicitly or retain tau on the right.

The source writes sin(90−theta) without a degree mark while the spring coordinate normally uses radians. Use cos(theta), or write sin(pi/2−theta) for radians; numerical spring torque always uses theta in radians.

The RP figure does not identify a horizontal reference axis. State theta1 measured from horizontal toward positive upward height, consistent with its positive g(m1 l1+m2 d2)sin(theta1) potential. This differs from the single-DOF downward-positive convention.

In the lower standalone M_x display, the character between Izz2 and m2 d2² resembles an underscore rather than a plus. Earlier K, the upper scalar torque and the upper full matrix equation all have a clear plus. Derive M11 from the positive kinetic-energy coefficient and disclose the inconsistent lower typography.

V denotes potential energy in the first summary line but a velocity-dependent generalized-force vector in the dynamic decomposition. Questions distinguish scalar U (or V_potential) from vector V_velocity and do not conflate them.
